issues.description: Class name mismatch: The UML diagram in the problem statement declares a class named 'Course', while the textual description and both template and solution code define and refer to a class named 'Lecture'. Problem statement (UML) uses 'Course' which could lead students to expect a class named 'Course' and follow its attribute order; template/src and solution/src both declare 'public class Lecture', use attribute names and constructor for Lecture. This inconsistency can confuse students about which class name and diagram to follow when implementing attributes and the constructor.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across artifacts. Rename the UML class in problem_statement.md from 'Course' to 'Lecture' so the diagram matches the textual description and code (attributes and constructor). Alternatively, if 'Course' was intended, rename the template and solution classes and all references from 'Lecture' to 'Course'. Ensure the UML, problem text, and template use the same class name so students unambiguously implement the correct class.

issues.description: The UML diagram in the problem statement declares the class as 'Course', while the provided template and solution Java files declare the class as 'Lecture'. Problem statement: 'Course' (UML class). Template: public class Lecture (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java). Solution: public class Lecture (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java). This mismatch makes it unclear which identifier students should implement or map to the UML diagram and may cause confusion when following the instructions that repeatedly refer to a Lecture class.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Either rename the UML class in problem_statement.md from 'Course' to 'Lecture' so it matches the textual description and both template and solution code, or rename the class in the template and solution from 'Lecture' to 'Course' and update all textual references. Prefer renaming the UML to 'Lecture' to align with the exercise wording and existing code.
